title: B2B Software / Technology
description: Committee purchase, long cycle, the product is invisible. The creative problem is making an abstraction concrete without resorting to a screenshot nobody can read on a phone.

purchase_triggers: a new leader with a mandate

objection_library: prove ROI before I ask for budget
angle_library: adoption story from a peer company

creative.image_style: abstract-but-legible product metaphor, generous negative space, restrained two-colour palette, diagrammatic clarity, no literal dashboard screenshots
creative.image_negative: unreadable UI screenshot, stock businesspeople, glowing brain, circuit-board cliché, robot hand touching screen
creative.video_style: screen-recorded proof intercut with a narrated point; the demo IS the hook

plays.title: Objection teardown series
plays.when: Sales reports a recurring objection, or win/loss data names a blocker.

with.structure: objection -> why it is reasonable -> the actual mechanics -> proof -> what to do next

plays.title: Case study to multi-channel proof
plays.when: A customer result is verifiable and the customer has consented to be named.

prompt_fragments.voice: You are writing for someone who evaluates tools for a living and has been disappointed before. Name the workflow, name the role, name the number. Skip the category-definition paragraph entirely.
prompt_fragments.proof_instruction: Prefer a customer name and a measured delta over an adjective. If the metric is not in the brief, describe the mechanism instead of inventing a figure.
prompt_fragments.visual_instruction: Render the CONCEPT of the workflow, not the interface. Diagrammatic, two accent colours maximum, wide margins, reads at thumbnail size.
prompt_fragments.objection_instruction: Address the security and migration objections explicitly whenever the audience includes IT or procurement — silence on those reads as evasion.
